quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #2
										  					
  

60 Questions • Passing Score 50

questions.question: Can cell phones distract drivers?
questions.explanation: Drivers should not use cell phones while driving. Do not use computers or other distracting devices. You can only use a phone to report a crash or emergency. Focus all your attention on driving.

questions.question: Do octagonal signs mean you must stop?
questions.explanation: A stop sign is red with white letters and shaped like an octagon. When you see a stop sign, come to a complete stop before the crosswalk or stop line. Only go when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They tell drivers about situations ahead. This sign warns you that the right lane is ending. Be ready for traffic to merge.

questions.question: When you hear a fire engine siren behind you, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down until it passes you.
Pull over to the side of the road and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear an emergency vehicle siren, pull over to the curb or side of the road right away and stop.

questions.question: When passing another car, should you wait until you see the entire car in your rearview mirror before moving back to the right lane?
questions.explanation: After passing a car, wait until you can see the whole car in your rearview mirror before returning to the right lane.

questions.question: What is the best way to avoid hydroplaning?

options.text: Slow down when roads are wet or slushy.
Watch out for standing water or puddles.

questions.explanation: On wet roads, cars need more distance to stop and may skid on turns. Do not use cruise control in wet or icy conditions. Slow down and drive carefully.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: A yellow triangle with black lettering means no passing zone. It appears on the left side of a two-way, two-lane road where you cannot pass other cars.

questions.question: If you are angry after an argument, what should you do before driving?

options.text: Play loud music so you won't think about it.
Take a few minutes to calm down.
Drive on the highway to release stress.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to calm down.
questions.explanation: Your emotions affect how safely you drive. If you are angry, excited, scared, worried, or sad, calm down before driving. You need to focus completely on the road.

questions.question: If you drive faster than other cars on a two-lane road and keep passing them, what will happen?

options.text: You will arrive much faster and safer.
You will increase your chances of a crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will increase your chances of a crash.
questions.explanation: Avoid passing on two-lane roads. Every time you pass another car, your risk of a crash goes up.

questions.question: When you see other drivers acting angry, what should you do?
questions.explanation: When other drivers are angry, distance yourself from them. Do not look at them or make gestures that could upset them. Slow down, move over, or do whatever is safe to stay away from danger.

questions.question: Smoking while driving:
questions.explanation: Smoking while driving takes your hands off the wheel and your eyes off the road. This is dangerous.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign warns of a roundabout ahead. Slow down and yield to traffic already in the roundabout.

questions.question: Which of the following commonly causes traffic crashes?

options.text: Speeding or driving too fast for conditions.
Getting enough rest and staying alert.
Watching the road and paying attention.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speeding or driving too fast for conditions.
questions.explanation: Speeding and driving too fast for road conditions cause many accidents. Always drive at a safe speed that matches traffic and road conditions.

questions.question: If you leave your vehicle unattended, you must:

options.text: Lock the ignition and remove the key.

questions.explanation: When you leave your vehicle, turn off the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, and set the parking brake.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Bad weather means you need to change how you drive.
Slow down when driving in rain and fog.
Watch for fast vehicles behind you in bad weather.

questions.explanation: Bad weather requires you to adjust your driving. Slow down in rain and fog. Be aware of vehicles behind you that may be driving too fast for the conditions.

questions.question: It is unlawful to:

options.text: Pass another vehicle in a no passing zone.
Pass another vehicle at a railroad crossing.

questions.explanation: You cannot pass in no passing zones, on hills, in curves, or where you cannot see ahead safely. You cannot pass at street crossings, railroad crossings, or in work zones.

questions.question: Before changing lanes, you should:
questions.explanation: Check both mirrors for traffic behind you. Then look over your shoulder to check for vehicles in your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: The left lane is for vehicles with a certain number of people.
Specific turns are allowed from specific lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left lane is for vehicles with a certain number of people.
questions.explanation: This is a high occupancy vehicle (HOV) lane. It is reserved for buses and vehicles with multiple passengers, as shown on the sign.

questions.question: Drinking alcohol and driving is:

options.text: Safe if you only have a few drinks.

questions.explanation: Drinking and driving is a serious safety problem. You cannot drive safely after drinking alcohol. It puts you and others at risk.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, you should:
questions.explanation: Tired driving is as dangerous as drunk driving. If you feel tired, stop driving immediately.

questions.question: Mixing alcohol with drugs can:
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol and drugs can strengthen the effects of both substances. Driving after consuming alcohol or drugs is unsafe. Mixing them together is even more dangerous.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: Wet roads are slippery and dangerous. This sign warns you to slow down. It takes longer to stop on wet pavement.

questions.question: Tailgating (driving too close to another car's rear bumper):

options.text: Can make other drivers angry and frustrated.
Cannot result in a traffic ticket.
Prevents other drivers from cutting you off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can make other drivers angry and frustrated.
questions.explanation: Tailgating is unsafe and can lead to aggressive driving. You can receive a ticket for driving unsafely.

questions.question: As your blood alcohol level (BAC) increases, you become:
questions.explanation: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) measures the percentage of alcohol in your blood. The higher your BAC, the more impaired you become.

questions.question: You cannot drive within ____ of an emergency vehicle with its siren on.
questions.explanation: Stay away from emergency vehicles (ambulances, fire trucks, police cars) that are using sirens or flashing lights. It is illegal to follow within 500 feet of an active emergency vehicle.

questions.question: You must signal before turning, changing lanes, or pulling away from a curb:

options.text: Only if other cars are nearby.
Always. It is the law and good driving practice.
Only during the move, not before.
Not needed if you move slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always. It is the law and good driving practice.
questions.explanation: Signal at least 100 feet before you turn or change lanes. Always signal before pulling away from a curb to warn other drivers.

questions.question: Your brake lights tell other drivers that you:
questions.explanation: Brake lights signal that you are slowing down or stopping. Keep your brake lights working at all times.

questions.question: If you are in a serious crash, you should:
questions.explanation: Stop your vehicle if possible and move off the road. Call 911 if anyone is injured. Report the crash to police if there is an injury, death, or more than $1,000 in property damage (or more than $200 in damage to government property like signs).

questions.question: Orange signs are used in construction work zones.
questions.explanation: Construction zone signs are usually orange and diamond-shaped. Many are reflective to be easier to see at night.

questions.question: White pavement markings separate traffic moving in opposite directions.
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: An intersection has no traffic signs or signals. You arrive at the same time as a vehicle on your right. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up and go through the intersection.
Slow down and let the vehicle on your right go first.
Drive into the intersection and make the other vehicle stop.
Honk your horn and drive through.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let the vehicle on your right go first.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way. Let it pass safely before you go through.

questions.question: You are borrowing a car you have never driven before. What should you do?

options.text: Not worry about it because all cars are the same.
Hide the fact that you are unfamiliar with the car.
Ignore any obvious problems to avoid embarrassing your friend.
Spend a few minutes learning where controls are and how they work before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spend a few minutes learning where controls are and how they work before driving.
questions.explanation: Before driving an unfamiliar car, take time to find and understand the turn signals, headlights, wipers, brakes, gear selector, and horn. Fix any problems before you drive.

questions.question: Wearing both a lap belt and shoulder strap increases your survival chances by three to four times in a crash.
questions.explanation: A lap belt alone doubles your survival chances. A lap belt and shoulder strap together increase your chances three to four times.

questions.question: Why should you not stop suddenly in front of large trucks and buses?

options.text: Small vehicle drivers cannot see large trucks and buses in their mirrors.
Large trucks and buses need more distance to stop because of their size and weight.
Large trucks and buses travel faster than small cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks and buses need more distance to stop because of their size and weight.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles need longer distances to stop than smaller cars. A sudden stop in front of a large vehicle may cause a crash because the driver cannot stop in time.

questions.question: The best way to change lanes is:

options.text: When a car is in your blind spot.

questions.explanation: Always change lanes slowly and carefully. Only change lanes when you need to. Every lane change increases the risk of an accident.

questions.question: Safe passing requires cooperation between two drivers.
questions.explanation: Safe passing requires both drivers to work together. Do not speed up when someone is passing you. Do not cut back in too close after passing.

questions.question: Nighttime is the safest time for cyclists to ride their bikes.
questions.explanation: Bicycles are hard to see in the dark, even with lights and reflectors. Both drivers and cyclists must be extra careful at night to prevent crashes.

questions.question: You can start to pass in a passing zone even if you will not finish before the zone ends.
questions.explanation: You must finish passing before you reach a no passing zone. It is unsafe to be in the middle of a pass when you enter a no passing zone.

questions.question: If a tire blows out while you are driving, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the car straight and slow down by easing off the gas pedal.
Keep your speed and steer straight.
Swerve back and forth to warn traffic behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the car straight and slow down by easing off the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel tight and keep the car straight. Ease off the gas pedal. Do not brake until you have control. When safe, brake gently and move to the side of the road.

questions.question: How can drivers drive more safely in winter weather?
questions.explanation: Winter driving is dangerous. On slippery roads, drive slower, turn and stop gently, and keep a larger distance between your car and other cars.

questions.question: When you see a railroad crossing warning sign, what should you do?

options.text: Be ready to stop if a train is coming.
Find a way around any lowered gates.
Assume no train is coming and drive normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop if a train is coming.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossing warning signs warn drivers that a train may be coming. Always obey these signs. Never go around barriers or ignore the warning.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means U-turns are not allowed here.

questions.question: What does a posted speed limit sign show?

options.text: The exact speed you must drive to avoid a ticket.
The maximum safe speed in good road and weather conditions.
The maximum safe speed in all road conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum safe speed in good road and weather conditions.
questions.explanation: A speed limit sign shows the highest legal speed for that road. You may need to drive slower than the posted limit if conditions are bad. When weather or road conditions are poor, slow down.

questions.question: What do "No passing zone" signs tell drivers?

options.text: It is not safe to pass another car.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is not safe to pass another car.
questions.explanation: A "No passing zone" sign means you cannot pass other cars in that area. These zones have limited visibility, making it unsafe to pass.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: A five-sided yellow or yellow-green sign warns you of a school zone or school crossing.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They get you ready for road hazards. This sign warns that traffic will merge from the right. Be ready to let them merge safely.

questions.question: What should you do when you meet an aggressive driver?

options.text: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
Cut them off to slow them down.
Show them you don't like their driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Stay calm if another driver is aggressive or dangerous. Put distance between your car and theirs. Slow down and let them pass. Do not make eye contact or make rude gestures.

questions.question: Seat belts work best when worn by:

options.text: Everyone in the car, every time you drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Everyone in the car, every time you drive.
questions.explanation: All people in a car should wear a seat belt. In a crash, a person without a seat belt becomes a dangerous flying object that can hurt others in the car.

questions.question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, you must:

options.text: Follow what the crossing guard tells you to do.
Do what other cars do, even if the guard says something different.
Assume the guard should not be directing traffic.
Follow the normal rules as if no children were there.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow what the crossing guard tells you to do.
questions.explanation: Slow down and follow directions from signs, crossing guards, or police officers. Always drive carefully in a school zone.

questions.question: You do not have to follow directions from a flagger in a construction zone.
questions.explanation: You must follow directions from signs, flaggers, and police officers. Ignoring a flagger is illegal and dangerous to construction workers.

questions.question: How can you avoid becoming an aggressive driver?

options.text: Stay calm and focus on driving.
Drive faster than the posted speed limit.
Follow the car in front of you too closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay calm and focus on driving.
questions.explanation: To avoid aggressive driving, stay calm and focus on your driving. Don't take other drivers' actions personally. Plan extra travel time, follow speed limits, and be patient with other drivers on the road.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Stop only if cars are coming.

questions.explanation: This sign shows that bicycles cross or travel along this road. Drive slowly and carefully in this area because cyclists may be present.

questions.question: When you see a steady red traffic light, what should you do?

options.text: Drive through if no other cars are coming.
Keep driving because you have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is nearby.

questions.explanation: A steady red light means you must stop completely. Driving through a red light is illegal and dangerous. You may turn right on red only if there is no sign forbidding it.

questions.question: How does alcohol affect your driving skills and judgment?

options.text: It improves driving skills but harms judgment.
It harms both driving skills and judgment.
It does not affect driving skills or judgment.
It harms driving skills but not judgment.

questions.correctAnswerText: It harms both driving skills and judgment.
questions.explanation: Alcohol reduces reaction time and makes it harder to see clearly. It also affects your ability to judge speed and distance. Alcohol lowers your caution and makes you more likely to take risks.

questions.question: What happens if you mix alcohol with prescription or over-the-counter medicine?

options.text: The medicine weakens the alcohol's effects.
Alcohol helps the medicine work better.
The two together can greatly increase the effects of both.
They have no effect on each other.

questions.correctAnswerText: The two together can greatly increase the effects of both.
questions.explanation: Alcohol and other drugs together can multiply their effects. For example, one drink combined with cold medicine could affect you like several drinks alone would.

questions.question: When driving past parked cars, what should you do?

options.text: Be ready for a person or car to suddenly move into your lane.
Expect other drivers and pedestrians to respect your right-of-way.
Honk to warn drivers and pedestrians.
Drive fast to avoid hitting pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for a person or car to suddenly move into your lane.
questions.explanation: Keep distance between your car and parked vehicles. Someone may step out of a parked car or between cars. A parked car may pull out suddenly. Drive slowly and watch for pedestrian and driver movement.

questions.question: Dashed lines between lanes mean you cannot pass other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Solid lines mean you cannot pass. Dashed lines mean you may pass if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: When driving in fog, which headlights should you use?
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, or snow. High beams bounce off these conditions and make it harder to see.

questions.question: How can you prevent highway fatigue or boredom?

options.text: Change your speed slightly now and then.
Keep your eyes moving across the road.

questions.explanation: Long drives can cause boredom and fatigue. Start your trip well-rested. Take regular breaks even if you are not tired. Keep your eyes scanning the road to avoid staring in one spot.

questions.question: Drivers must be careful when passing large vehicles and should not stay beside them for long.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles have large blind spots on both sides. Do not drive beside them for long. It is safer to move ahead or drop back.
